summary: Swift was ported by the guide (version 3.2). That means a naming hook (Naming_swift.ts, 24 lines), a provider (Syntax_swift.ts, 171 lines), the porter's part of the forms file (+32/-5), and the three old components deleted (764 lines). The provider has no notes. No shared file was touched. Build exit 0 and the tree is clean after it. Guard and reader: 5/5 pass. Golden: 2/2. Suite without lanes: 2596 pass, 0 fail, 5 skipped. The final one-command run (REGEN=1) gives PORTCHECK PASS, exit 0. The SCRATCH=1 run fails as expected for a language nobody reviewed. Swift's toolchain is absent here, so none of the 172 changed blocks (47 tutorial, 19 root, 106 reference) is compiled. The swift README test only checks structure. Swift is the first port with result style 'wrapped', so its wrapped sentences in shared runtimeprose had never been printed by any language. They are now printed and were read once, but no reference language exists to compare against.

interface_gaps.construct: The wrapped result style's REFERENCE return clause and the create comment state the record read (record(f, bound)) but never the unwrap. With record '.data()' the page said 'Returns a value holding the entity ... `.data()` reads its record', which is false for swift (a Value has no data()).
interface_gaps.file_line: ts/src/helpers/runtimeprose.ts:142 (carries) and :207-208 (returnClause 'wrapped'); OLD ReadmeRef_swift.ts:32 named the unwrap
interface_gaps.smallest_change: Have the wrapped branches of returnClause/carries say '... which `${unwrap}` takes out'. Then record can stay '{var}.data()'.
interface_gaps.providers_forced: none (swift is the only wrapped provider). It counts as breaking only because it changes a sentence
interface_gaps.worked_around: Yes, and openly: facts.record is declared as '({var}.asNative as? Entity)?.data()'. This is real code that reads the record from the bound Value, so every record sentence is true. In the tutorial it is redundant next to the unwrap clause. The guard re-derives only the name 'data' from it, not the unwrap part

interface_gaps.construct: A printer may not concatenate onto a description name, so the old `<var>Entity` binding for the unwrapped entity cannot be printed. The print printer instead shadows the name: `if let ambient = ambient.asNative as? Entity { print(ambient.data()) }`
interface_gaps.smallest_change: Additive: an optional layout.vars-style name for the unwrapped entity supplied by the hook. Not needed
interface_gaps.worked_around: no; shadowing in an inner scope is legal Swift (not compiled here)

interface_gaps.construct: The client printer uses an option's key as a variable name for a map-valued option (`let server = VMap()`, `let feature = VMap()`). This is safe only because the shared option keys are identifiers
